name: 2026 Iran war (US and Israel vs Iran)
started: 2026-02-28 (US Operation Epic Fury and Israeli Operation Roaring Lion; current phase since ceasefire collapse on 2026-07-08)
summary: A US-Israeli air war on Iran that began on 28 February 2026 killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and much of Iran's security leadership. Iran answered with thousands of missiles and drones at Israel, US bases and every Gulf monarchy, and closed the Strait of Hormuz. A June peace memorandum collapsed in July, and by late October the two sides are in an armed stand-off with no ceasefire and threats of a second round after the US midterms.

sides.name: United States and Israel
members: US Air Force bomber force (B-1, B-2, B-52)
US Navy carrier strike groups Abraham Lincoln, Gerald R. Ford, George H.W. Bush
backers: Gulf states (basing and air defence; Qatar, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain shot down Iranian missiles, drones and aircraft)
United Kingdom (basing for B-1 and B-52; RAF Typhoon intercepts over Qatar)
sides.strength: Three US carriers in theatre by 8 Mar 2026; 2,500 Marines of the 31st MEU arrived 28 Mar; 62 bomber missions by early April including 18 round trips from the US (Wikipedia 2026 Iran war; NDTA/Business Insider, Apr 2026)

sides.name: Iran and the 'Axis of Resistance'
members: Popular Mobilization Forces and Islamic Resistance in Iraq
backers: China (main buyer of oil; Chinese-owned ships given passage)
leaders: Mojtaba Khamenei (Supreme Leader from 8 Mar 2026, wounded)
Mohsen Rezaei (head of Supreme National Security Council by Sep 2026)
sides.strength: US intelligence (NYT, 12 May 2026) judged Iran kept about 70% of its mobile missile launchers and of its pre-war missile stockpile, and had regained access to about 90% of underground missile sites

background: After the June 2025 twelve-day war and the US bombing of Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan, talks on Iran's nuclear programme stalled while Iran still held roughly 440 kg of uranium enriched to 60 percent, enough for about ten weapons if further enriched (IAEA). On 28 February 2026 the United States and Israel launched a joint campaign aimed at Iran's missiles, navy, air defences, nuclear sites and leadership. Khamenei was killed on day one and his son Mojtaba was named Supreme Leader on 8 March.

The war matters far beyond Iran. Iran's strategy was to spread the pain: it fired more projectiles at the UAE, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Jordan and Oman than the public record shows at Israel, hit Qatar's Ras Laffan LNG complex, and shut the Strait of Hormuz, through which about a fifth of the world's oil normally passes. The war has drained US and Gulf missile-defence stocks, pushed Brent above 100 dollars, re-ignited Lebanon and Yemen, and left Iran's enriched uranium unaccounted for.
year: Oct 2025 to Feb 2026: no open war; nuclear diplomacy (the IAEA joined US-Iran talks in February) failed. 28 Feb: Operation Epic Fury and Operation Roaring Lion struck more than 1,000 targets in 24 hours; the Israeli Air Force used over 1,200 bombs on about 500 targets; Khamenei was killed; B-2s flew 37-hour missions from the US; four US troops died when a missile hit a command post, and a Kuwaiti F/A-18 mistakenly shot down three US F-15Es. 1 to 3 Mar: Iran hit THAAD radars in Jordan, the UAE and Saudi Arabia, hit Ras Laffan, Bahrain, Kuwait and Riyadh; Hezbollah joined; Qatar shot down two Iranian Su-24s and an Israeli F-35I shot down a Yak-130. 4 Mar: USS Charlotte sank the frigate IRIS Dena off Sri Lanka (104 dead). Mid-March: US struck Kharg Island's military sites (14 Mar); Israel killed Ali Larijani and the Basij chief (17 Mar) and the intelligence minister (18 Mar) and hit South Pars; Iran struck Ras Laffan, knocking out 17 percent of Qatar's LNG exports; US bunker-busters hit Natanz and Iran hit Dimona (21 Mar). 27 Mar: Iranian missiles damaged US tankers and an E-3 at Prince Sultan Air Base. 28 Mar: the Houthis joined. Early April: Iran shot down an F-15E and two A-10s; a 155-aircraft rescue lost two C-130s. 8 Apr: two-week ceasefire; CENTCOM said 13,000+ targets had been struck. 12 to 13 Apr: Islamabad talks failed; US imposed a naval blockade of Iran. 7 to 8 Jun: Iran fired missiles at Israel after Israeli strikes on Beirut, and Israel struck targets around Tehran, Tabriz and Isfahan and damaged the Karun petrochemical complex at Mahshahr. 17 Jun: Trump and Pezeshkian signed the Islamabad Memorandum, lifting both blockades. 8 Jul: after tankers were hit near Oman, the US struck 80+ targets including 60 IRGC boats and declared the ceasefire over; about 13 nights of strikes followed and Iran fired at US bases in Bahrain and Kuwait. Late July to August: strikes paused for Omani mediation; Trump cancelled one strike round. 5 Sep: Iran fired ballistic missiles at a US carrier and destroyer, which evaded them; the US wrecked three Iranian tankers. October: the most intense month of attacks on shipping; Trump said he would not attack before the 3 Nov midterms but floated 'another little Epic Fury'.
situation: As of late October 2026 there is no ceasefire in force but also no sustained air campaign. The US Navy blockades Iranian oil exports and Iran keeps Hormuz closed to most shipping, with mines and missiles hitting tankers. Trump has said he will not strike Iran before the 3 November midterms; the Pentagon is reportedly planning for renewed heavy fighting afterwards if ordered, and on 27 October the Wall Street Journal reported that Washington had told Gulf states to prepare for a short, intense campaign, with a Patriot battery moving from Texas and another carrier group due in November. Trump has not decided. Diplomacy runs mainly through Qatar, which reportedly delivered a new draft deal on 25 October that an Iranian official called 'unacceptable', and through a letter from Vice President Vance to Mohsen Rezaei proposing an early meeting, which Tehran had not answered by 29 October. Qatari mediators returned to Tehran on 30 October for talks coordinated with Washington, and Iran was expected to answer a revised proposal by the end of the week; Tehran still demands the blockade and oil sanctions be lifted first. A Pentagon estimate given to Congress on 28 October put the US cost of the war above 47 billion dollars, and Defense Secretary Hegseth removed the Joint Staff's strategy chief, Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, over alleged leaks about the war. On 30 October the Pentagon raised the US death toll to 23: 11 killed by enemy fire and 12 in non-hostile incidents.
technical: Day one scale: 1,000+ targets in 24 hours and 'tens of thousands' of munitions in 57 hours (Pentagon, 2 Mar); about 2,000 aimpoints in the first days at roughly one munition per aimpoint.
Israeli Air Force day one: about 500 targets and 1,200+ bombs in 24 hours, its largest sortie ever.
Bombers: 62 missions by B-1, B-2 and B-52 by early April, including 18 round trips of 30+ hours from the US; B-1s and B-52s flew from UK bases; B-52s first overflew Iran on 30 Mar.
Tomahawks were the 'first shooters at sea', fired by destroyers including USS Spruance and USS Thomas Hudner; no total count has been published.
First combat use of LUCAS, a US one-way attack drone copied from Iran's Shahed-136, by Task Force Scorpion Strike; HIMARS, ATACMS and PrSM used, with 'virtually all' ATACMS and PrSM expended (CBS).

Bunker-buster strikes hit Natanz on 21 Mar; Arak and Ardakan damaged 27 Mar; Isfahan struck 30 Mar; explosions at Bushehr's auxiliary building 4 Apr. No public confirmation of GBU-57 counts or B-21 use in 2026.

Iranian launch rate collapsed fast: ballistic missiles fell from 480 on day one to 40 by 10 Mar, drones from 720 to 60 (about -92%, analyst AJ Jaff). Iran shifted to fewer, heavier missiles with 1,000 kg+ warheads.

Israel front: about 650 Iranian ballistic missiles were fired at Israel in the 40 days to the 8 Apr ceasefire, falling from about 90 on day one to 10 to 15 a day; about 66 got through (16 unitary, 50 cluster), per IDF figures reported by Wikipedia.

Cluster warheads: about half of the first 300 missiles and most of the 650 carried cluster warheads, each scattering dozens of submunitions over roughly 10 km; bomblets killed people in Yehud, Ramat Gan, Tel Aviv and Bnei Brak, which is why many Israeli deaths came from outdoor exposure rather than direct hits.

Israeli layered defence: Arrow 2/3 against ballistic missiles, David's Sling against medium-range missiles and drones, Iron Dome against short-range rockets; no interception percentage or Israeli interceptor stock data has been published.
Iran's resilience: US intelligence in May judged about 70% of mobile launchers and missile stocks survived and 90% of underground sites were back in use.

Gulf volumes: UAE faced 378 ballistic missiles, 15 cruise missiles and about 1,835 drones by 27 Mar; Kuwait 237 missiles and 445 drones by 10 Mar; Bahrain 132 and 234 by 18 Mar; Qatar 203 and 87 by 18 Mar; Saudi 38+ and 435 by 18 Mar; Jordan intercepted 108 of 119 on 7 Mar.

Interceptor depletion: CSIS estimates US Patriot stock fell from 2,200 to 2,330 before the war to 759 to 827 by end July, and THAAD from 452 to 234 to 278; CNN sources said nearly four-fifths of THAAD was used (disputed by Hegseth). Rebuilding takes until at least 2029.
Gulf Patriot stocks: JINSA estimated the UAE and Kuwait had used about 75% and Bahrain up to 87% by 29 Mar.
Iran struck THAAD radar sites in Jordan, the UAE and Saudi Arabia on 1 to 2 Mar, destroying at least one, an attempt to blind the regional missile shield.
Air combat: Qatari F-15s shot down two Su-24s (first Qatari air-to-air kills); an F-35I shot down a Yak-130 over Tehran; an RAF Typhoon downed a drone over Qatar.

US aircraft losses: 98 lost or damaged by May, including three F-15Es to Kuwaiti friendly fire, one F-15E and two A-10s to Iranian fire, two C-130s destroyed in a rescue, and tankers and an E-3 damaged at Prince Sultan Air Base.

Decapitation: killed leaders include Ali Khamenei, Ali Larijani, Basij chief Gholamreza Soleimani, Intelligence Minister Esmaeil Khatib, IRGC Navy chief Alireza Tangsiri (Israeli claim), missile chief Makram Atimi, IRGC intelligence chief Majid Khademi and Quds Force commander Yazdan Mir.
Naval: Iranian frigate IRIS Dena sunk by the submarine USS Charlotte off Sri Lanka (104 dead); CENTCOM claimed 130 Iranian vessels struck by 19 Mar and 60 IRGC small boats on 8 Jul.

Nuclear material: IAEA counts 440.9 kg of 60% enriched uranium, about 200 kg believed in tunnels at Isfahan, unverified since June 2025; a newly declared Isfahan enrichment plant was apparently not hit.
Cost asymmetry: a Shahed-136 costs about 50,000 dollars against about 4 million dollars for a Patriot interceptor.

Energy war: Israel's strikes on South Pars petrochemicals were claimed to take 85% of Iran's petrochemical exports offline; Iran's strike on Ras Laffan cut 17% of Qatar's LNG exports for an estimated 3 to 5 years.
casualties: Iran: 3,528 killed and 27,170 injured (Iranian government); 3,684 killed including 1,249 military and 1,721 civilians (HRANA); 3,400+ civilians killed (OCHA); the US and Israel claim 6,000+ Iranian military dead. Israel: 40 soldiers, 1 contractor and 31 civilians killed, 7,841 injured (another Wikipedia page counts 28 deaths inside Israel from Iranian fire). US: 23 service members dead, 11 by enemy fire and 12 in non-hostile incidents (Pentagon casualty system via CBS News, 30 Oct 2026), plus 1 contractor; 861+ wounded (May 2026). Gulf: UAE 16 killed and 246 injured; Kuwait 12 killed and 190 injured; Bahrain 2 killed; Saudi Arabia 3 killed; Qatar 1 killed; Oman 18 killed at Sohar and Bukha. Iraq 119+ killed by April. Most figures were compiled in spring 2026 (Wikipedia compilations of official and NGO data) and undercount summer and autumn fighting.
displaced: UNICEF reported hundreds of thousands displaced inside Iran (spring 2026); more than 70,000 Afghans returned from Iran in the first two weeks of March, many under pressure (NYT via Wikipedia). No consolidated figure for late 2026 was found.

outlook: The US midterm elections on 3 November are the hinge. Watch for a second US-Israeli strike package after that date, Iranian ballistic missile salvoes at US ships and Gulf bases, and whether depleted Patriot and THAAD stocks shape the decision. Diplomatic channels run through Pakistan and Oman; any deal would have to settle the fate of the Isfahan uranium, which the IAEA cannot verify.

battles.name: US punitive strikes on Hormozgan after ceasefire collapse
battles.place: Bandar Abbas, Sirik and Qeshm Island, Hormozgan, Iran
sides: IRGC Navy and coastal defences; IRGC missile and drone forces
battles.outcome: 80+ targets hit on the first night including 60 IRGC small boats; about 13 consecutive nights of strikes before Trump paused for Omani mediation. Iran claimed attacks on 85 US sites in Bahrain and Kuwait, with no damage reported.
battles.forces: US strike aircraft hitting air defences, coastal radars, anti-ship missile sites, drone launch sites and port infrastructure.
battles.losses: 60 IRGC small boats claimed destroyed on 8 July; one IRGC Navy member killed at Bandar Mahshahr (Tasnim).
battles.significance: Ended the Islamabad Memorandum and restarted the US blockade and oil sanctions, setting up the long autumn stand-off.

battles.name: F-15E shootdown and combat search and rescue
battles.place: Southern Iran near the Strait of Hormuz (exact sites not published; approximate)
sides: US Air Force and special operations rescue forces
battles.outcome: F-15E crew recovered (weapons officer after 48 hours) but at heavy cost in aircraft.
battles.losses: 1 F-15E and 2 A-10s shot down, 2 C-130s destroyed, helicopters damaged; 3 IRGC members killed (Wikipedia).
battles.significance: The first US F-15E lost to enemy fire in over 20 years; showed Iran's air defences were degraded but not destroyed.

battles.place: Al Taweelah, Abu Dhabi, UAE (approximate position)
battles.outcome: Severe damage and a full shutdown; repairs could take up to a year.
battles.forces: The UAE had faced 378 ballistic missiles, 15 cruise missiles and about 1,835 drones by 27 March.
battles.significance: One of the world's largest aluminium plants knocked out, part of Iran's campaign to make the war costly for Gulf economies.

battles.name: Iranian missile strikes on Dimona and Arad
battles.place: Dimona and Arad, Southern District, Israel
battles.outcome: Iran said it targeted the Shimon Peres Negev Nuclear Research Center, but missiles hit residential areas of Dimona and Arad.
battles.losses: At least 47 injured in Dimona and 71 in Arad, 10 seriously (Wikipedia, Israel in the 2026 Iran war; the main war article gives 78+ injured at Dimona).
battles.significance: A symbolic tit-for-tat for the US strike on Natanz the same day, aimed at Israel's own nuclear site.

battles.name: Israeli strikes on South Pars gas field and petrochemical plants
battles.outcome: Gas field hit on 18 March and petrochemical plants on 6 April; the IAF claimed 85% of Iran's petrochemical exports were knocked offline. Iran retaliated against Qatar's LNG plants.
battles.significance: Opened an energy war in which both sides targeted gas and petrochemical infrastructure that serves world markets.

battles.outcome: Ali Larijani and Basij commander Gholamreza Soleimani killed on 17 March; Intelligence Minister Esmaeil Khatib killed on 18 March.
battles.significance: Part of a decapitation campaign that also killed the IRGC Navy chief, the missile chief, the IRGC intelligence chief and a Quds Force commander, hollowing out the organisations that run internal security and the missile war.

battles.name: Iranian strikes on Ras Laffan LNG complex
battles.outcome: QatarEnergy halted all LNG output on 2 March and declared force majeure; the 18 March strike disrupted 17% of Qatar's LNG exports with repairs estimated at 3 to 5 years.
battles.forces: Two drones on 2 March (Ras Laffan and Mesaieed); a larger strike on 18 March in retaliation for Israel's South Pars attack.
battles.losses: Major damage to LNG trains; no strike casualty figure given (Wikipedia).
battles.significance: The single most damaging blow to global gas supply in the war, tying Qatar's economy directly to the conflict.

Iranian leadership, IRGC, air defences, missile and naval forces
battles.outcome: Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and other senior officials killed; more than 1,000 targets struck in 24 hours; local air superiority declared.
